subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Should OpenShell enforce a bounded-read contract through the existing safe read primitive, and what supported maximum size should that contract expose?
rationale: The branch changes a sandbox resource boundary and introduces a user-visible failure mode for reads above 100 MiB; maintainers must choose the durable limit rather than accept an arbitrary cap.

options.title: Adopt bounded safe reads
options.body: Replace the stat-then-read sequence with the existing safe read path using an explicitly chosen `maxBytes` value and add focused boundary tests.

options.title: Keep unbounded reads
options.body: Reject the cap if OpenShell intentionally guarantees unrestricted sandbox file reads, accepting the associated host-memory exposure.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded safe reads
recommendation.body: Replace the stat-then-read sequence with the existing safe read path using an explicitly chosen `maxBytes` value and add focused boundary tests.
